subject: Request: endpoint spend-waterfall tile + SLO/billing correlation
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New console ask — endpoint spend-waterfall + SLO correlation

Hi team,

Acme asked for a compact way to understand "what exactly drove spend" for a given endpoint over a billing window, and to quickly see whether the same events triggered SLO breaches. The ask should work for both hosted and Dedicated tenants.

High-level goal: one small dashboard card (tile) you can pin to any tenant or route that shows a waterfall of spend breakouts for the selected window and the top 3 call-path contributors (by token-cost). The card should also mark timestamps where SLOs (latency or availability) were violated and surface a probable correlation score.

Key constraints from product:
- Must be queryable by route_id / model_variant / tenant_id.
- 7-day rolling window default, with quick presets (24h, 7d, 30d).
- Drill action: click waterfall bar -> open trace/call-path playback for that group.
- Lightweight: responses should be sub-second for common queries (approx p50).

Can Diego and Soojin sketch a minimal data contract and an initial UX wire so we can show Acme next week? I attached a quick spreadsheet with proposed fields.

Owners / asks:
- Diego: feasibility & required telemetry (which traces/events we need).
- Soojin: mockups + microcopy for the tile (what metrics, how to show correlation).
- Marcus/Grace: any regulatory or billing-ops concerns if we expose this on Dedicated tenants.

Deadline: internal sketch by EOD Wednesday, customer sync Friday.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New console ask — endpoint spend-waterfall + SLO correlation

Thanks Rachel — this is a good framing. A few quick notes after a skim of the spreadsheet and last week's telemetry postmortem: 

1) Minimal telemetry we need (per request):
   - route_id, model_variant, tenant_id, request_id, token_count_in, token_count_out, model_name, timestamp, compute_seconds (or GPU_ms), kv_cache_hit (bool), batching_group_id (if any).
   - A lightweight sampled call-path id that allows grouping requests into contributing prompt/templates. We already emit a hashed_prompt_id in some flows; we can extend that.

2) Correlation approach:
   - We'll compute an hourly time series: spend_by_hour and p95_latency_by_hour. Correlation score = pointwise Pearson over the selected window + an anomaly flag when spend spike and p95 spike align within a 1-hour lag.

3) Performance notes:
   - For tenants with very high request volumes we should rely on pre-aggregations (hourly, per-route, per-model_variant). Ad-hoc one-off investigations can hit the sample store.

4) Dedicated tenants: make sure all pre-aggregations can be configured to run in-customer VPC or use a retained export to the tenant's analytics bucket — Marcus & Grace, can you confirm acceptable patterns?

I'll mock a sample payload and attach a short log extract to illustrate call-path grouping. If we keep the default window to 7d and use hourly pre-agg, p50 queries should be quick.

Diego
Senior Observability Engineer

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New console ask — endpoint spend-waterfall + SLO correlation

Quick UX stub attached (see Drive link). My proposal for the tile (keeps it compact):
- Top line: selected entity (tenant / route / variant) + window selector.
- Left: stacked waterfall (compute / output tokens / input tokens / batching overhead) with hover breakdown.
- Right: small timeline with p50/p95 pctl lines and vertical markers for SLO breaches. Hover shows correlation score and list of top 3 call-path IDs.
- Drill: open a side-panel with call-path playback (sample request payload, tokens, model variant, cost estimate).

Microcopy suggestion: "Estimate shown uses sampled call-paths and pre-aggregates; click for raw traces."

Open question for product: do we label the waterfall categories as "billing buckets" or "cost contributors"? Billing team prefers the former for clarity with invoices.

Soojin
Product Designer

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New console ask — endpoint spend-waterfall + SLO correlation

This looks great — thanks all. Quick decisions and next steps: 

Decisions:
- Use the label "cost contributors" in the product UI, but billing docs will map each contributor to invoice line-items.
- Default window 7d, with 24h and 30d presets.
- Pre-aggregation: hourly per route/model_variant on-host (hosted) and as a configurable job (Dedicated).

Action items (owners):
- Diego: drop a short spec of the telemetry extension and the sample payload by EOD Thursday. Attach the sample-call-paths.log to the JIRA ticket CONSOLE-1987.
- Soojin: refine mock, include accessibility notes and the microcopy change; draft two compact variants (one for small-team tenants, one for enterprise tenants) by next Tuesday.
- Marcus & Grace: confirm Dedicated deployment pattern & privacy constraints; Marcus to sync with infra/legal by Monday.
- Rachel: prepare a 10-minute demo script for the Friday customer sync and include the Drive link + JIRA in the invite.

I'll update the JIRA and send the calendar invite. If anyone sees a privacy red flag in the call-path sample (PII risk), flag immediately and we'll pivot to hashed/sampled payloads only.

Rachel
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced: spend-waterfall-spec.xlsx, sample-call-paths.log
